# `screen_companies`

**Screen a list of companies**

Screens up to 50 companies at once and returns one row each: status, age, and which signals were found. Built for the list-of-suppliers question — paste the names or numbers from a spreadsheet and get back the rows worth looking at. Names that match more than one company are never guessed at; they come back under `unresolved` with their candidates so you can ask. Anything skipped for want of rate-limit budget comes back under `not_screened` with the reason, so the table is never quietly shorter than the list you passed in. Rows carry signal codes only — call company_snapshot on a company number for the detail behind them. Officers are excluded by default because they cost an extra request per company; sections_used says what the signals could see.

This tool reads only and changes nothing, and calls an external service (the Companies House API).

## Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `companies` | string[] | yes | Company names or numbers. Mixed input is fine. Maximum 50 per call. |
| `include_officers` | boolean | no | Fetch officers too, enabling the no_active_officers and recent_officer_departures signals. Off by default: it adds one request per company. |
| `include_charges` | boolean | no | Include charges. On by default. |
| `include_insolvency` | boolean | no | Include insolvency cases. On by default. |

## Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `requested` | number | yes | — |
| `sections_used` | string[] | yes | Signals in this table can only reflect these sections. Officers are off by default. |
| `screened` | object[] | yes | — |
| `screened[].input` | string | yes | What was passed in, so rows can be matched back to the source list. |
| `screened[].company_number` | string | yes | — |
| `screened[].name` | string | yes | — |
| `screened[].status` | string | no | — |
| `screened[].incorporated_on` | string | no | — |
| `screened[].age_years` | number | no | — |
| `screened[].signal_codes` | enum (12 values)[] | yes | — |
| `screened[].signal_count` | number | yes | Call company_snapshot on the number for the detail behind these. |
| `unresolved` | object[] | yes | Inputs that could not be resolved to exactly one company. Never guessed at. |
| `unresolved[].input` | string | yes | — |
| `unresolved[].reason` | string | yes | — |
| `unresolved[].candidates` | object[] | no | Ask which was meant, then screen the chosen number directly. |
| `unresolved[].candidates[].company_number` | string | yes | Use this for every other tool in this server. |
| `unresolved[].candidates[].name` | string | yes | — |
| `unresolved[].candidates[].status` | string | no | active, dissolved, liquidation, administration, and so on. |
| `not_screened` | object[] | yes | Inputs deliberately skipped, with the reason. Nothing is dropped silently. |
| `not_screened[].input` | string | yes | — |
| `not_screened[].reason` | string | yes | — |
| `meta` | object | yes | Provenance and budget for this answer. |
| `meta.cached` | boolean | yes | Answer came from the local cache rather than a live request. |
| `meta.stale` | boolean | yes | Answer came from an expired cache entry because Companies House was unreachable. Treat the data as possibly out of date. |
| `meta.age_seconds` | number | no | How long ago the cached answer was retrieved. Absent for a live answer. |
| `meta.rate_limit_remaining` | number | yes | Requests still available in the current five-minute window. Pace long runs by this. |
| `meta.rate_limit_resets_in_ms` | number | yes | Milliseconds until more budget becomes available. |
| `meta.licence` | `"OGL-v3.0"` | yes | Companies House data is Open Government Licence v3.0. |

On failure the tool returns `isError: true` and a payload carrying `code`,
`message`, `next_step` and `retryable` instead of the fields above. See
[the error reference](README.md#errors).
